dedupe_keys.name: ipea access to opportunities project aop accessibility to jobs health education and social services by transport mode for 20 brazilian cities

description: The Access to Opportunities Project (AOP) publishes high-resolution estimates of how easily people in Brazil's largest cities can reach jobs, public health services, schools and social assistance centres by each transport mode. It is led by the AOP-Lab of the Institute for Applied Economic Research (Ipea), Brazil's federal economic research institute, which releases all its publications, data and code openly. Coverage: the 20 largest Brazilian cities, with accessibility by car, walking and cycling for all of them and by public transport for over nine cities, for 2017, 2018 and 2019. Data on an H3 hexagonal grid give travel-time-based accessibility indicators such as opportunities reachable within time limits and time to the nearest facility, population by sex, race, income and age, and the locations of jobs, schools, health care facilities and social assistance reference centres (CRAS). Format and access: web explorer and downloads on the Ipea site and the aopdata R package on CRAN, which returns tables or spatial objects; free. Licence: aopdata package MIT; project code GPL-3.0-or-later or MIT; data terms on the Ipea site (not stated on the pages read). Caveats: estimates are for fixed years and set departure times, public transport results depend on the quality of each city's GTFS, and the latest year is 2019. Simulation uses: baseline accessibility and social vulnerability layers for network flow, capacity planning and emergency response studies of urban transport and critical services. Related records: r5r (model-r5r), also from Ipea, is the routing engine used to compute the travel times.
